sentences.text: Daemonosaurus was an extinct dinosaur that lived during the Late Triassic period in New Mexico.
This animal possessed a deep, shortened skull equipped with large teeth and a rounded eye socket.
Its dentition included prominent, fang-like structures designed for gripping prey.
Unlike many early dinosaurs which typically had four, this species had only three teeth in its upper front jaw.
The very first tooth at the front of the upper jaw was the longest tooth in the entire skull.
These upper front teeth were straight at their base but curved at the top.
The lower jaw held an estimated ten curved and serrated teeth.
In the lower jaw, the second tooth was the largest, followed by a large first tooth set back from the tip, with the rest decreasing in size towards the rear.
This creature represents a lineage from the earliest dinosaur radiation that persisted alongside South American forms like Eoraptor and Herrerasaurus until the end of the Triassic.
Fossil evidence suggests the animal died after being washed into a pond and drowned during a sheet flood event.
The species was named by Sues, Nesbitt, Berman, and Henrici in 2011.
The name Daemonosaurus means "demon reptile" derived from Greek words.
The species name chauliodus means "prominent toothed" referring to its forward-pointing front teeth.
The holotype specimen was discovered in a sediment block from the Coelophysis Quarry at Ghost Ranch, New Mexico.
The fossil block containing the holotype was collected in the early 1980s by E.H. Colbert.
The holotype specimen was first uncovered by a volunteer while the block was on loan to the State Museum of Pennsylvania.
The only known fossil of this animal consists of a skull and neck fragments found at Ghost Ranch.
Sues estimated Daemonosaurus to be around 1.5 meters long based on related theropod proportions.
Holtz estimated Daemonosaurus was at most 2.2 meters long and weighed between 9.1 and 22.7 kilograms.
A large oval hole behind the rib articulations in Daemonosaurus has been equated with pneumatic pockets seen in other dinosaurs.
The type species of the genus Daemonosaurus is Daemonosaurus chauliodus.
Daemonosaurus is classified as a basal theropod situated outside the Neotheropoda clade.
Phylogenetic analysis found Daemonosaurus chauliodus to be closely related to Tawa hallae.
Daemonosaurus differs from Herrerasaurus by having much larger teeth in the premaxilla and distinct skull features.
Daemonosaurus is distinguished from Eoraptor lunensis by possessing much larger premaxillary and anterior maxillary teeth.
Daemonosaurus differs from Chindesaurus bryansmalli based on features of its cervical vertebrae.
Nesbitt and Sues (2020) considered Daemonosaurus a likely saurischian but could not conclusively place it within any specific dinosaur subgroup.
Recent studies recovered Daemonosaurus in a clade named Morphoraptora alongside Tawa, Chindesaurus, and Ptychotherates.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Daemonosaurus as Saurischia.
Daemonosaurus lived during the Late Triassic, specifically the Rhaetian stage or possibly the latest Norian stage.
The animal lived between 205.7 and 201.4 million years ago.
Two hundred million years ago, the habitat of Daemonosaurus near the equator featured a warm, monsoon-like climate with heavy seasonal rain.
Daemonosaurus lived alongside early neotheropods like Coelophysis during the Late Triassic.
It is debated whether Daemonosaurus is a basal theropod or a non-theropod basal saurischian.
A 2026 study proposed the clade Morphoraptora to group Daemonosaurus with Tawa and other herrerasaurians.
